item.title: Kanmangafuchi Abyss: A Row of Mossy Jizo Statues Beside a Gorge — Guide
item.description: Kanmangafuchi Abyss is a scenic volcanic gorge formed by an eruption of nearby Mount Nantai, carved by the Daiya River into striking columnar basalt formations. Along the riverside path stand a row of roughly 70 weathered stone Jizo statues (guardian deities of travellers and children), each wearing a red knitted cap, with a local legend claiming it’s impossible to count the same number twice. The quiet, moss-covered setting offers a peaceful contrast to Nikko’s more crowded shrine complex.
